title: Government plans to phase out brick kilns within seven to eight years
excerpt: Environment minister Abdul Awal Mintoo told parliament that kilns will be replaced by blocks. Drives since February shut 136 kilns.

image.alt: A brick kiln chimney rising over waterlogged fields in Kurigram
image.credit: Tanvir Rahat / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The government plans to phase out about 8,000 brick kilns gradually over the next seven to eight years and increase the production of environment-friendly blocks, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo told parliament on Wednesday (18 November), The Business Standard reported, citing BSS.

He was replying to a call attention notice from Khairul Kabir Khokon, MP for Narsingdi-1. Between February and October this year, the minister said, authorities ran 205 mobile court drives, filed 435 cases, collected Tk 10.20 crore in fines and shut 136 kilns. The country has 31 air quality monitoring stations, he said.

In Bandarban, none of the district's 73 brick kilns has approval or environmental clearance, the Department of Environment told Bonik Barta in a report published on Wednesday. Reporters saw child labour at kilns in Faitong, Lama, and residents said kilns cut hills and dam canals. Mobile courts imposed fines of Tk 71.46 lakh between September and early November and sent arrest requests for 12 accused, the paper reported.

Why it matters

Brick kilns are a major source of winter air pollution and employ large numbers of seasonal workers, many of them in debt bondage to kiln owners. A phase-out affects health, environment and livelihood programmes at the same time.

What to watch

Whether the plan comes with a timeline by district, support for kiln workers who lose seasonal work, and enforcement as the winter kiln season starts.
